transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-03 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (DeltaEdge Head of Search), Lena Ortiz (DeltaEdge ML Eng), Tom Hsu (CTO), Riley (PM)
- Recording: yes

Summary: 30-min product walkthrough of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints focused on DeltaEdge's e-commerce search use case. Covered demo of API calls, console routing, simple reranker pipeline, cost/latency tradeoffs, and integration options (hosted vs VPC). Agreed next steps and data share for pilot.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we can wait one minute for tom to hop on if needed, but looks like most of us are here so i'll kick off. hello deltaedge team, i'm avery with redwood inference, i'm the ae here.
00:20 Speaker 2 (Samir): hey avery, yeah thanks for scheduling. we want to see a practical walkthrough — embeddings plus rerank — for our product search. latency and cost are our big constraints.
00:33 Speaker 1 (Avery): great, that's exactly what we'll show. marco from solutions will do the deep parts. i'll take quick qualification questions, then hand over for a live demo.
00:45 Speaker 3 (Marco): hey all, marco here. quick agenda: 1) short architecture + hosted API endpoints; 2) embedding flow + nearest-neighbor retrieval; 3) reranker endpoint demo with a small query set; 4) console and Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization; 5) Q&A.
01:10 Speaker 2 (Samir): just to be clear, are we demoing hosted only today or also private / vpc?
01:18 Speaker 3 (Marco): primarily hosted today — we will call out differences for VPC/private at the end. hosted is where most teams start and it's fast to prototype.
01:25 Speaker 4 (Lena): our infra team is worried about PII and retention — do you have SOC-2 and KMS integration?
01:31 Speaker 1 (Avery): yes, we are SOC 2 Type 2 compliant, and we support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers. i'll drop the security deck link after.
01:40 Speaker 4 (Lena): ok thanks.
01:44 Speaker 3 (Marco): i'll pull up the notebook. so first, embedding flow: you call the /embeddings endpoint, we return vector arrays, store them in your vector DB — faiss, milvus, or a managed provider — and at query time you do an ANN search then call our /rerank endpoint to rescore the top N.
02:15 Speaker 5 (Tom): when you say rerank endpoint, is that an LLM re-ranking with context or a separate model?
02:23 Speaker 3 (Marco): good q. rerank is our hosted API route that runs a supervised reranker or a cross-encoder model variant depending on the template. technically it's a model variant in our catalog optimized for pairwise scoring; it's cheaper than full generation because it returns scores and short explanations. sometimes it's a small transformer cross-encoder.
02:48 Speaker 2 (Samir): what's the typical latency for rerank on hosted for top-10 reranks?
02:54 Speaker 3 (Marco): on hosted we see p95 around 70-180ms for top-10 depending on model and sequence length; for very low-latency you can use our smaller reranker family or move to a dedicated pool.
03:10 Speaker 2 (Samir): okay that seems reasonable. cost ballpark?
03:15 Speaker 1 (Avery): i'll go over pricing after the demo — we'll tailor to your qps.
03:20 Speaker 6 (Riley): can you show the actual API call? code snippet?
03:24 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes. switching to the live notebook. (30s typing noise)
03:45 Speaker 3 (Marco): here's a snippet: POST /v1/embeddings with text:'red running shoes' returns vector 1536-d floats (or quantized variants). then offline index with hnswfaiss and at query time ANN returns ids and distances. then we take top 25 and call POST /v1/rerank with inputs: query + candidate passages, get back scores.
04:24 Speaker 4 (Lena): do you handle batching client-side or do you recommend Redwood Optimize to set server-side batching?
04:32 Speaker 3 (Marco): Redwood Optimize recommends batching and autosuggests batch size based on your latency SLO and token distribution. hosted runtime also does continuous batching behind the scenes but Optimize helps tune parameters to reduce cost without breaking SLOs.
04:58 Speaker 2 (Samir): what about KV cache? we have long session contexts for personalization.
05:05 Speaker 3 (Marco): We manage KV cache for generation flows; for rerank it's usually pairwise scoring so KV isn't a big factor. in other places in the transcript you might see it transcribed as 'KV cash' in older exports, you'll see some typos.
05:20 Speaker 1 (Avery): quick pause — tom, you had questions about integrating with our auth?
05:25 Speaker 5 (Tom): yes, SSO and role-based access. we need SAML, SCIM user sync and RBAC for routes, plus audit logs to comply with SOC2.
05:36 Speaker 1 (Avery): we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC at API key and team level, and audit logs retained per your plan. private deploys can push logs to your SIEM. we'll attach the security whitepaper.
05:52 Speaker 3 (Marco): back to demo — i'm going to run a live rerank on a small product set; heads up transcription might drop a few words.
06:00 Speaker 3 (Marco): (typing) submitting top-25 candidates... tops shown. the reranker returns scores and a short 'why' explanation field. example: 'because it matches color and size filters and has high sales velocity' — note those 'why' explanations are model-generated; for compliance you can disable or redact them.
06:35 Speaker 4 (Lena): is the 'why' deterministic? we need reproducible scoring for A/B tests.
06:42 Speaker 3 (Marco): it's deterministic per model checkpoint if you fix temperature and the reranker variant. we recommend pinning model versions in the deployment config.
07:00 Speaker 2 (Samir): what about embeddings drift over time, do you support re-embedding pipelines?
07:08 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, typical pattern: re-embed batches during off-peak hours, store version metadata, use aliasing in the index to roll forward. Optimize can recommend re-embedding cadence based on query distribution.
07:25 Speaker 6 (Riley): any demo of the Console?
07:30 Speaker 3 (Marco): switching to Redwood Console. (mouse clicks) here you can see per-route latency, token cost, token breakdown. here's a suggestion card from Optimize: "Lower batch size from 16 to 8 for lower p95 tail in region eu-west-1" — these cards are auto-suggested after a short profiling run.
08:05 Speaker 1 (Avery): quick note: our Optimize suggestions also include quantization recommendations — for heavy read workloads you can use a 4-bit quantized embedding model; Optimize simulates the cost change.
08:20 Speaker 4 (Lena): does quantized embeddings affect retrieval accuracy much?
08:27 Speaker 3 (Marco): small delta for many product catalogs, but we run an eval set to measure. we can help run an A/B on your eval set.
08:38 Speaker 2 (Samir): can you show error rates and fallback? we need graceful degradation during incidents.
08:45 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes — in Console you can configure fallback routing: if a primary model is saturated, route to a cheaper variant or different region, and we have canary rollouts. we also instrument traces per request ID.
09:05 Speaker 5 (Tom): what about data residency? we have EU customers and need some data to stay in-region.
09:12 Speaker 1 (Avery): hosted supports region pinning (eu-west-1, us-west-2, ap-southeast-1). for strict residency we recommend Private deployment (VPC) where your data never leaves your network.
09:28 Speaker 6 (Riley): okay can we talk about expected ops work to test in our staging?
09:33 Speaker 3 (Marco): minimal. for hosted you get API keys, set up ingestion, and a small evaluation harness. we usually ask for a prioritized query set and some ground-truth relevancy labels. for a pilot we can run the reranker offline against your logs and give MAP/NDCG numbers.
10:02 Speaker 2 (Samir): that would be helpful.
10:05 Speaker 3 (Marco): i'll demo an offline evaluation quickly — i'm uploading a 200 query sample now. (upload noise)
10:22 Speaker 3 (Marco): results showing: baseline elasticsearch mean NDCG@10 0.48, reranker run via Redwood hosted 0.63 on this small sample — again sample is small, but it's indicative.
10:38 Speaker 4 (Lena): those are promising. what drives the perf gap — model understanding vs dense retrieval?
10:45 Speaker 3 (Marco): a mix — embeddings + ANN get you candidate recall, reranker uses cross-attention to resolve subtle relevance like variant matching and promotional boosts. also negative mining and training the reranker on click logs improves performance.
11:05 Speaker 2 (Samir): how do you handle personalization? we have user vectors and want to blend into reranker scoring.
11:12 Speaker 3 (Marco): you can include user vector as an additional input to the rerank endpoint, or precompute user-aware features. we provide SDK helpers for feature concatenation.
11:28 Speaker 6 (Riley): can we control the rerank scoring formula? like apply business weights?
11:34 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, highest-level approach: reranker returns scores and you can post-process them, or we support hybrid models where you add categorical features such as boosted_promotions to inputs. we also support a final rule-based filter layer in the pipeline.
11:50 Speaker 1 (Avery): i'll pause and check for procurement/legal type questions — tom?
11:55 Speaker 5 (Tom): licensing: monthly commit or pay-as-you-go? we expect spiky traffic around launches.
12:02 Speaker 1 (Avery): we offer hosted pay-as-you-go and committed capacity options via Redwood Dedicated; we can include burst credits for launches. pricing tier will be in the follow-up.
12:18 Speaker 4 (Lena): is there a free trial or credits?
12:22 Speaker 1 (Avery): yes, we can provide pilot credits.
12:26 Speaker 3 (Marco): back to live demo — i'm going to show the API response shapes. (keystrokes) POST /v1/rerank returns an array of scores and optional 'explain' strings. sometimes model text in explain has small hallucinations — we advise using explain for debugging only.
12:50 Speaker 2 (Samir): any guardrails to reduce PII leakage from explain fields?
12:55 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes you can disable explain, and we offer content filters and PII redaction options across hosted and dedicated.
13:10 Speaker 1 (Avery): quick breath — would you all like to see a small live AB between two reranker variants?
13:15 Speaker 2 (Samir): yes please.
13:18 Speaker 3 (Marco): running A/B now — variant A is our default cross-encoder small, variant B is a tuned cross-encoder trained on ecom click pairs.
13:40 Speaker 3 (Marco): results after 200 pairs: B improves click-thru simulated metric by ~8% at top 3. again, small sample.
14:02 Speaker 4 (Lena): how long to onboard reranker training with our logs?
14:08 Speaker 3 (Marco): roughly 2-4 weeks for a pilot depending on data cleanliness and labels. we can help with data pipelines.
14:20 Speaker 6 (Riley): who owns the model training — you or us?
14:24 Speaker 3 (Marco): flexible — we can train models for you in-hosted pipelines, or provide training recipes to run in your infra, or a hybrid where we run model tuning jobs in a dedicated environment.
14:40 Speaker 2 (Samir): can we do edge caching for hot queries?
14:45 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, Console supports cache rules for high-frequency queries and prefix caching for partial-match patterns.
15:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): i'll fast-forward a bit — Console and Optimize also expose cost breakdown by token and per-route. (screen share brief)
15:20 Speaker 5 (Tom): our security team will ask for audit logs and retention policy.
15:26 Speaker 1 (Avery): we'll include the SOC2 + retention docs. same with KMS integration steps.
15:35 Speaker 3 (Marco): another quick demo: you can run a model compatibility check in Console — it simulates expected latency for your median seq length and suggests a quantization profile. here it suggests 4-bit for embedding encoding and a 16-bit reranker.
16:00 Speaker 4 (Lena): sometimes the embeddings drift for some languages — how's multilingual support?
16:07 Speaker 3 (Marco): we have multilingual embedding variants; Optimize can suggest a multilingual vs monolingual model based on query language distribution.
16:20 Speaker 6 (Riley): any production stories?
16:24 Speaker 1 (Avery): we have customers in retail seeing 15-30% improvement in top-5 click-through and 20% reduction in cost using reranker + Optimize.
16:35 Speaker 2 (Samir): nice.
16:38 Speaker 3 (Marco): wrapping up demo — open to questions, but i want to stress next steps: send pricing, reranker quickstart notebook, and request deltaedge sample logs.
17:02 Speaker 6 (Riley): can you send the notebook link now?
17:06 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes — link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart/embeddings-rerank (will email too).
17:18 Speaker 4 (Lena): for the pilot, can we scope a POC that runs on our staging dataset with 50k products?
17:25 Speaker 1 (Avery): absolutely, that's a common size. we'll propose a pilot scope: 4-week pilot, hosted API + reranker, two evaluation gates (offline NDCG + online shadow traffic), deltaedge commit TBD.
17:40 Speaker 5 (Tom): what about SLA for hosted?
17:45 Speaker 1 (Avery): hosted has an SLA for uptime on enterprise plan; Dedicated has stricter p99 latency commitments. we'll put exact numbers in the quote.
17:56 Speaker 2 (Samir): ok sounds good.
18:00 Speaker 3 (Marco): quick ask — if you can drop a sanitized sample of query logs and some relevance labels, we can run an offline evaluation and return a short report.
18:10 Speaker 2 (Samir): will do.
18:13 Speaker 6 (Riley): timeline to start pilot? next week?
18:18 Speaker 1 (Avery): we can start provisioning keys and credits next week once you sign an MSA for pilot — i'll send a pilot MSA template.
18:30 Speaker 3 (Marco): final Qs?
18:35 Speaker 4 (Lena): curious about retraining cadence — how often do you recommend?
18:40 Speaker 3 (Marco): depends on catalog churn — for heavy catalogs weekly or biweekly; for stable catalogs monthly. Optimize flags when reranking performance drops.
18:55 Speaker 2 (Samir): ok thanks, this was helpful.
19:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): recap and next steps: 1) Avery sends pricing and pilot MSA; 2) Marco shares notebook and sample prompts; 3) DeltaEdge to send sanitized logs and evaluation set; 4) schedule 60-min technical deep dive in one week.
19:25 Speaker 5 (Tom): all good from my side.
19:28 Speaker 6 (Riley): thanks everyone.
19:30 Speaker 1 (Avery): thanks all — we'll follow up.
